title: Six-year follow-up of a world record-breaking master marathon runner
authors: Romberger NT, Stock JM, McMillan RK, Overstreet ML, Lepers R, Joyner MJ, Farquhar WB
population: One male distance runner, retested at age 76 after setting the men's over-70 marathon world record in 2018
findings: Between 2018 and 2024 marathon running velocity decreased significantly.
VO2max declined by 15.1%, HRmax by 3.2% and maximal O2 pulse by 12.4%, suggesting reduced maximal stroke volume and/or arteriovenous O2 difference.
Running economy remained similar to 2018, and he likely still runs marathons at about 90% of VO2max.
The performance decline is attributed primarily to reduced VO2max, speculated to reflect primarily age-related processes.
limitations: Single-subject case study of an elite outlier; not generalisable; the 6-year interval spans ages about 70-76.
implications: Consistent with modelling decline in the 70s mainly via VO2max/threshold paces with running economy unchanged; no change beyond the existing model is justified.
When observed HRmax falls over years, lower the HRmax parameter accordingly (HRmax fell 3.2% over 6 years here, one person).

verification.notes: Crossref and Europe PMC abstract match; numbers verbatim.
